items.action: Upgrade FortiMail to 8.0.2, 7.6.7 or 7.4.9+ immediately; 7.2 users must migrate to 7.4+. Internet-facing appliances should be checked against Fortinet's IOCs (rogue liblog.so, ld.so.preload entries) — patching does not evict an existing implant.
items.details: Fortinet disclosed the flaw on Oct 1 in advisory FG-IR-26-175 (path traversal + NULL-byte neutralization in the IBE request handler), confirmed in-the-wild exploitation as a zero-day, and CISA added it to the KEV catalog the same day. Attackers are using the file-write to implant persistent linker preloads and backdoor services on mail appliances.
items.summary: Fortinet confirms CVE-2026-104286 (CVSS 9.8) — an unauthenticated arbitrary file write in FortiMail's Identity-Based Encryption handler — is being actively exploited as a zero-day.
items.title: FortiMail zero-day CVE-2026-104286 under active exploitation

items.action: Upgrade to NetScaler ADC/Gateway 14.1-73.46+ or 13.1-64.29+ (FIPS 14.1-73.46) as soon as possible.
items.details: The memory overflow flaw's impact depends on configuration — deployments running NetScaler as a SAML service provider or identity provider face both remote code execution and denial-of-service risk. Citrix says it is not aware of attacks in the wild so far.
items.summary: Citrix patched CVE-2026-107406 (CVSS 9.5), a critical memory-overflow flaw in NetScaler ADC and Gateway that can lead to remote code execution or DoS under specific configurations.
items.title: Citrix patches critical NetScaler RCE CVE-2026-107406

items.action: Inventory Nexus 3000/9000 switches running NX-OS and Smart License On-Prem/Manager installs; plan the October security-hardening updates now — several flaws score 9.8–10.0.
items.details: Highlights: Nexus 3000/9000 MPLS OAM RCE (CVE-2026-76465, 9.8), NGOAM RCE trio (CVE-2026-76485/86/76501, 9.8), NX-API RCE (CVE-2026-76471, 9.8), plus Smart License On-Prem CVEs rated 10.0 (CVE-2026-76480 series). Under Cisco's risk-based disclosure, advisories publish on the first and third Wednesday of each month.
items.summary: Cisco's October security bundle packs a stack of Critical advisories for NX-OS (9.8 RCEs via MPLS OAM, NGOAM and NX-API), Smart License On-Prem (CVSS 10.0) and APIC.
items.title: Cisco October bundle: Critical 9.8–10.0 RCEs hit NX-OS and licensing gear

items.details: The listing, spotted Oct 9 on the Ransomware.live tracker, ties the exposure to the 'Cavalier' infostealer family. HudsonRock-linked reporting puts 615 employee accounts, 10,808 user accounts and 1,134 third-party credentials at risk, with ParanoidLab flagging ~300,000 exposed passwords. No official Deloitte statement on this specific claim yet.
items.summary: Thegentlemen ransomware group listed Deloitte on its leak site on Oct 9 — an unverified claim linked to Cavalier infostealer activity, per dark-web trackers.
items.title: Thegentlemen ransomware group names Deloitte on its leak site

items.details: The alleged loot includes tens of thousands of medical faxes (2022–2026) with patient names and diagnoses, methadone clinic records under 42 CFR Part 2, 47,602 medical-assistance files with driver licenses and SSN cards, county payroll registers and jail gang-intelligence files.
items.summary: Rhysida claims Anne Arundel County, Maryland, listing 814,500 files (2.6 TB) — including background-check dossiers with full SSNs, medical faxes and payroll registers.
items.title: Rhysida claims Anne Arundel County: 2.6 TB of citizen data on the block

items.details: BYOD says it got in through an employee of Liberty Mobile, the MVNO behind Trump Mobile, via infostealer malware — and claims neither entity used MFA. The leaked data reportedly includes personal details of Eric Brunnett, the Trump Organization's CIO. Neither Trump Mobile nor Liberty Mobile has responded.
items.summary: The BYOD ransomware crew claims to have breached Trump Mobile and leaked customer names, emails, phone numbers, home addresses and order details for 3,615 people.
items.title: BYOD ransomware group claims Trump Mobile breach via MVNO employee

items.details: In the joint advisory with CSIRT-Fin, CERT-In says attackers compromise internet-facing apps and exposed APIs to steal payment gateway, aggregator and partner-bank credentials, then invoke fund-transfer APIs directly from the victim's whitelisted infrastructure — bypassing loan, KYC, beneficiary and transaction-limit checks. Entry points include unauthenticated APIs, unrestricted file uploads, static API tokens in source code and MFA-less remote services.
items.summary: CERT-In (advisory CIAD-2026-0046, Oct 9) warns NBFCs, fintechs and payment providers that attackers — possibly using AI-assisted offensive frameworks — are stealing payment API credentials and triggering direct fund transfers to mule accounts.
items.title: CERT-In warns NBFCs/fintechs of AI-assisted payment-API attacks

items.details: The claim appeared on the group's leak feed on Oct 8. As with all leak-site listings, the claim is unverified — neither the group nor IIT Roorkee has confirmed compromise scope so far.
items.summary: The UmBra ransomware group listed IIT Roorkee on its leak site — an unverified claim making one of India's premier technical institutes the latest education-sector target.
items.title: UmBra ransomware group claims IIT Roorkee

items.details: The flaws could expose election officials' contact details and allow reading or forging data in the app. CERT-In's reply reached Adhikary on the evening of Oct 6 — a day after HT sent both agencies questions — saying one flaw was fixed and the rest were 'under progress'.
items.summary: Security researcher Nisarga Adhikary says he warned ECI and CERT-In in July about flaws in the ECINET voter-services site and app; CERT-In has now fixed one flaw, with the rest under review.
items.title: ECINET flaws were flagged to ECI and CERT-In back in July, says researcher
